claimsToVerify: Roman public latrines had communal multi-seat stone benches with no partition walls
Running water channels beneath or in front of seating were used for rinsing or waste removal
The sponge-on-a-stick (tersorium) existed and was kept in buckets of water or vinegar
Modern scholarly debate questions whether the tersorium was for personal wiping or cleaning the latrine benches/facility
Evidence exists for the use of cloth scraps and ceramic sherds (pessoi) for personal wiping
Trapped methane gas in Roman sewer systems posed fire and explosion hazards
